page: Microsoft Azure D4d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs split across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), and AES-NI, with no hardware accelerators or GPUs included.

Memory and integrated storage follow standard balanced ratios. The instance supplies 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. Bundled with the instance is 161 GB of local SSD ephemeral storage. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on internal or assigned networking configurations for connectivity.

Benchmark results place the D4d_v4 in low-to-mid tier performance ranges. Single-core evaluations, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1332.0 and text processing, register in the middle 50% category, alongside single-threaded gzip compression at 25.16 GB/sec. However, multi-core metrics fall largely into the bottom 25%, shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2921.0, a PassMark CPU score of 4399.99, and multi-core stress-ng at 3700.14. Memory bandwidth drops to the bottom 10% for large uncached reads at 22.2 GB/sec, though cached small-block reads achieve 219.01 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4d_v4 provides a dense balance of compute, memory, and fast local temporary storage for standard business workloads. Given its modest throughput in parallelized workloads and database operations (1461.74 on PassMark), it is best aligned with general application serving, development and test environments, small enterprise microservices, and lightweight caching systems like Redis, where balanced vCPU and RAM density is more critical than raw multi-threaded compute speed.
